title: Broad complex tachycardia after cocaine
stem: Resus 3. A 28-year-old man came from a nightclub with palpitations and agitation after 'a lot of coke'. HR 180, BP 118/76, RR 24, SpO2 97%, temperature 38.1 °C. He is restless and sweating. The monitor shows a broad complex tachycardia.

phases.title: Assess
phases.goal: Adverse features? The toxidrome? Read the ECG.

phases.title: Treat
phases.goal: From the drug cart: settle him, and treat the broad complexes the cocaine way. Promptly.

phases.title: If he becomes unstable
phases.goal: Watch him. If he loses his pressure: cardiovert him yourself.

events.say: He becomes grey and confused. BP 78/44.
events.untreated: He became unstable and was never cardioverted.

events.say: He becomes grey and confused. BP 78/44.
events.untreated: He became unstable and was never cardioverted.

notes:
Checked against TOXBASE (UK National Poisons Information Service), RCUK tachycardia algorithm (2021; unchanged in 2025) and AHA 2023 toxicology focused update.

Cocaine blocks noradrenaline reuptake (sympathomimetic) and sodium channels (class I effect: broad QRS, VT). First treat agitation, hyperthermia and hypertension with benzodiazepines. Broad complex arrhythmias: sodium bicarbonate 8.4% 50 mmol IV (1–2 mmol/kg), repeat as needed; correct hypoxia, acidosis and potassium. Lidocaine is an option for VT; avoid class Ia/Ic drugs. Beta-blockers are avoided in acute cocaine toxicity (unopposed alpha stimulation; AHA now considers them less harmful than thought, but they are not first-line). Adverse features (shock, syncope, ischaemia, heart failure) → synchronised cardioversion.

Your notes (sympathomimetic 'confusion' station) say benzodiazepines, cooling and avoiding beta-blockers alone; this matches.

Amiodarone is the standard drug for stable monomorphic VT in RCUK; with cocaine, bicarbonate first.

ABCDE.t: Adverse features: pressure, chest pain, syncope, breathlessness
ABCDE.r: BP 118/76. No chest pain now, no syncope, chest clear.

ECG.r: Regular broad complex tachycardia at 180, QRS 160 ms: treat as VT.
ECG.mark: Identifies regular broad complex tachycardia: treat as VT

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Settle the agitation; sodium load for the broad complexes.

opts.r: Too much at once: titrate 5–10 mg to effect.

opts.mark: Sodium bicarbonate for cocaine-induced broad complex tachycardia

opts.r: Too little: 50–100 mL (1–2 mmol/kg), repeated to narrow the QRS.
Beta-blockers are avoided in acute cocaine toxicity: unopposed alpha effects can worsen hypertension and ischaemia.
Verapamil in VT can cause collapse.
A class Ic sodium-channel blocker worsens cocaine's sodium-channel toxicity.

opts.t: Check K and Mg on a gas; correct

opts.early: He still has a good pressure: drugs first.
opts.performHint: Sedated by a skilled operator. Pads, SYNC on, 120–150 J, CHARGE, ALL CLEAR, SHOCK.

qs.q: Why sodium bicarbonate in cocaine toxicity?
wrong: It binds free cocaine in the bloodstream for excretion

qs.q: First-line drug for cocaine agitation and hypertension?
Regular broad complex tachycardia of uncertain origin should be treated as…

wrong: Atropine 0.5 mg IV every 3–5 minutes, up to 3 mg

qs.q: Which sign suggests a sympathomimetic rather than anticholinergic toxidrome?

badge.name: Snow Blind
badge.flavor: Benzos for the brain, bicarbonate for the QRS, electricity if unstable.

cards.q: Cocaine-induced broad complex tachycardia: first drug?
cards.why: Sodium loading and alkalinisation counter sodium-channel blockade.

cards.q: Agitation and hypertension after cocaine are treated first with…

options: Dry skin, urinary retention, flushing, mydriasis
cards.why: Sweating separates it from anticholinergic toxicity.

cards.q: Regular broad complex tachycardia without adverse features (non-toxic): drug?
options: Atropine 0.5 mg every 3–5 minutes, max 3 mg

cards.q: Class of antiarrhythmic to avoid in cocaine toxicity?

options: Propranolol to slow the heart rate
cards.why: Heat comes from muscle activity; paracetamol does not help.
